meaning: a deck-building card game: each turn you play action cards from your hand, then buy one card for your deck; most victory points when the game ends wins
one question the engine asks a player: which action to play, what to buy, what to trash, discard or gain; about 22 kinds
the 10 action cards (out of the base set's 26) dealt for one game
dominion-v1's evolved priority lists: a fixed rule for every kind of decision, found by a genetic algorithm
the best portfolio-v2 genome whose required cards are in the kingdom; the reference opponent of every measure
learning to act from the results of one's own actions (here: won or lost games), not from correct answers
supervised learning of an expert's choices; rl-v1 started this way, rl-v2 deliberately does not
"blank slate": training from random weights with no examples or rules
training in steps with different opponents: self-play, then the bots, then the league
stage 1 ends when the score against the GA genome has not set a new best for 60 iterations
the network's probabilities over the legal answers to a decision
the network's guess of the final result from here, in [−1, +1]
proximal policy optimisation: a policy-gradient method that limits how far one update can change the policy (the clip)
make choices from games that went better than expected more likely, and the others less likely
how much better a decision turned out than the network expected; positive → reinforce, negative → discourage
generalised advantage estimation: advantages built from the chain of win estimates along a game, with a mixing factor λ
how spread out the policy's probabilities are; high = undecided / exploring, low = certain
how far one update moved the policy; PPO stops an update early when it gets too large
the mix of opponents in training; in stage 3: the GA base, the bots, az-v1, rl-v1, past snapshots and the network itself
a saved copy of the network at some iteration, used later as an opponent
taking the highest-probability answer; used in every evaluation (training games sample instead)
az-v1's 1,000 goal games against the GA base plus 1,000 head-to-head games against az-v1's best agent
the 95% confidence interval of a win rate; about ±3 points at 1,000 games
the best of many noisy evaluations is flattered by luck
